description: Curated terminology and sources for Parkinson's disease, including clinical trials, movement and non-movement symptoms, treatment, genetics, research, daily living and care-partner support. This pack is for information discovery and is not medical advice.

synopsis.overview: Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurological condition caused by loss of nerve cells that produce dopamine in a part of the brain involved in movement.
synopsis.manifestations: The main movement symptoms are tremor, slowness and muscle stiffness. Balance problems can develop, and non-movement symptoms may include sleep disturbance, loss of smell, depression, anxiety, pain, constipation and changes in memory or thinking.
synopsis.management: There is no cure. Medicines such as levodopa can improve symptoms, while physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech and language therapy and exercise support function. Some people may be considered for device-assisted treatment or deep brain stimulation.
synopsis.outlook: Symptoms generally progress over years, but the pattern and response to treatment vary. Many people initially respond well to treatment and have a normal or near-normal life expectancy, although increasing assistance and vulnerability to complications may develop later.
